title: Power Automate: direct triggers for desktop flows
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts and documented scheduling, licensing and governance statements are supported. It correctly distinguishes the Scheduled triggers preview from the broader roadmap plan. The data policy navigation is accurate but stops at the policy list rather than the classification control.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Scheduled triggers require the licensing and capacity for the selected attended or unattended run mode.
claims.quote: The licensing and capacity required for the selected attended or unattended run mode.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Automate Premium includes attended desktop automation.
claims.quote: this license includes the ability for users to register their workstation, to create unlimited desktop flows, and to execute their desktop flows in attended mode on their registered machine through an attended bot borne by the license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The licensing overview directs unattended desktop flows generally to Process licences or pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended, or licensing flows on their own without use licenses, subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, covering user licensing, unattended capacity licensing and pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Power Automate supports both user and capacity licensing. ... For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended ... subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: The Power Automate flow-run meter for desktop flows is documented as preview.
claims.quote: Power Automate flow runs (preview) ... Flow runs for premium cloud flows and desktop flows.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Desktop flow runs in pay-as-you-go environments are subject to the Power Automate flow-run meter, supporting a variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Desktop flow runs in a pay-as-you-go environment are charged as follows:

claims.claim: Attended desktop flow charges in pay-as-you-go environments depend on the running user's licence entitlements.
claims.quote: Attended runs follow the entitlements of the user running the flow. A user whose license includes attended RPA isn't charged; a user whose license doesn't include it is charged $0.60 per run.

claims.claim: Unattended desktop flow runs in pay-as-you-go environments are charged per run.
claims.quote: Unattended runs are charged at $3.00 per run regardless of any capacity assigned to the environment.

claims.claim: Tenant-level data policy procedures require the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policy procedures require Environment Admin permissions when the environment has no Dataverse database.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: Environment-level policies in environments with Dataverse require System Administrator instead.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern desktop flow modules.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business, or Blocked.

claims.claim: A data policy can manage both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors.
claims.quote: You can define a DLP policy that manages both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The desktop flow connector can be governed in data policies like other connectors.
claims.quote: The desktop flow connector can be governed in your policies like any other connector in all environments.

claims.claim: Adding desktop flow modules to data policies causes evaluation and suspension of noncompliant desktop flows.
claims.quote: When desktop flow modules are added to DLP policies, your tenant's desktop flows are evaluated against them, and they're suspended if they're noncompliant.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy in Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell creates a data policy from a policy definition object.
claims.quote: Creates a new DLP policy in the tenant by using the NewPolicy DLPPolicyDefinition object. ... New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy ... Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy reaches the data policy list.
claims.quote: Select Security in the navigation pane. ... under Settings, select Data and privacy. ... select the Data policy section. ... From the list of data policies, select a policy, and then select Edit Policy.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Move to Business' for the documented classification operation. The existing route is correct but stops at the policy list; the remaining steps are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/prevent-data-loss.
